name: Alien Hives
background:
The Alien Hives are a faction of aliens using biotechnology, made up of a variety of subspecies which come from the remote frontiers of the galaxy, hoping to recreate the Mother that shaped them.

When they first arrived, they were viewed as monstrous invaders, but after a long war of extermination, breakthroughs in communication led to a fragile peace. Now, the Hives must come to terms with the legacy of the First Contact War and decide how they are to adapt.
backgroundFull:
Born on the fertile but unstable world known as Ar’khsenos, the Alien Hives are made up of the species that specialised to survive the constant cycle of extinction on their world. This cycle would only find its end as an entity which they came to know as the Mother developed a way to transmit her memories into the various species of the Ar’khsenos.

These species lived together in harmony under her guidance for thousands of years in a period known as the Everbloom. This changed suddenly when the Mother died; the traumatic details of the event have largely been lost to time, but before she died, she gave the species of Ark’henos a final gift: seven massive creatures capable of travelling through space, each bearing one of her genetic offspring. These space-faring creatures came to be known as Hiveships, and her offspring were known as the Children.

Hivers travelled throughout the Frontier,seeking a world where one of the Children could flourish and grow to take the place of their lost Mother, but with little success. After centuries of failed efforts beyond the edge of charted space, their hopes were rekindled with the distant Radiance Cascade, which echoed the Mother’s dying cries in their ancestral memories. Many Hiveships set out for the Sirius Sector. Their arrival set off a series of conflicts with the factions there known as the First Contact Wars, as communication proved difficult and many assumed the Hives were hostile because of their alien appearance and nature. The Hivers soon were locked into a war of extermination with the various species of Sirius, which only concluded when the DAO Union discovered a means to communicate.

Peace provided its own challenges for the Alien Hives, as they soon found themselves confronted with several alien ideas and values that challenged the structure of their society. They strive to stand on equal footing with the other species of the Sirius Sector, protect their migratory routes and defend their seeded worlds. Some in the lower castes now demand new rights, undermining the harmonious working of their Hiveships, while certain Hive Lords still wage a long war against all the species of Sirius, fearing that the corrupting influence of outsiders might ultimately destroy their way of life completely.

How will your Hive adapt?

product.description: After travelling through a swathe of the Frontier, the Alien Hives reached the Sirius Sector. Their arrival set off a series of conflicts with the factions in Sirius, as communication proved difficult and many assumed the Alien Hives were hostile because of their alien appearance and nature.

Vradhez has served his Hive for a long time, first assisting the late Hive Lord, and now as the chief advisor to Prime Warrior Druzhak. As his scarred face can attest, he has fought in many battles and lost countless friends. He will go to any lengths and sacrifice anything for his people.

Tempering the most aggressive tendencies of the Hive Lords on Hiveship Ikhanoz’s council, Snatcher Lord Nisuv views cooperation as essential to the Hives’ prosperity in Sirius, an extension of the Mother’s teachings, saying that the best fights are the ones that never happen.

Snatchers are a peculiar species, even within the very diverse population of the Hives. Their psychic abilities and skill for infiltration has caused some to see them as untrustworthy or devious. However, Snatcher Lord Nisuv is a shining example of the opposite.

Prime Warriors embody the strength and determination of the Hive, guiding their fellow Hivers at the forefront of work and warfare. They are most easily spotted by their horns, which serve to amplify their psychic sensitivity, allowing them to pick up distant signals and pass on orders from the Hive Lords, even when operating far away.

As a Prime Warrior, Druzhak was destined from birth to focus on war, leaving existential questions to the Hive Lord who led his people. However, the Hive sustained terrible losses during its migration through hotly contested territories, and Druzhak found himself leading the survivors.

He is a fearless combatant who takes his duty towards his people extremely seriously. He has seen many battles and has the scars to prove it, but all the death and pain he has witnessed weighs heavily on his soul.

Despite his reputation as a brute, Troseis is an ingenious Prime Warrior, whose obsession with digestion led him to a bio-weapon known as the Bileburner. This is because he would eat so much of whatever material he could get his claws on that his body responded by developing incredibly fierce digestive fluids.

With the help of other fellow Hivers, Troseis managed to design the Bileburner, which can project streams of corrosive acid onto foes. This did not earn him a lot of popularity at the beginning, as he was assigned to the defense of the insides of Hiveship Okhredoz.

Ksi’adoz belongs to Hiveship Voithsor, one of the most secretive that dwells deep within the Sirius Sector. Travelling silently across the dense, hostile environment of the Foreign Confines, Voithsor Hivers rely on stealth while shying from conflict and even contact. Instead, they seeded remote and hidden worlds, while harvesting discretely from backwater systems. The Voithsor Council has long held that their species’ best chance at survival is to be as close to invisible as possible.

product.description: The Devourer Titan is an even larger strain of the Devourer Beast, dwarfing its smaller cousin. Its immense appetite is one few Hives can sustain for long, often driving it to battle fury as it swipes aside enemy fortifications and formations in search of food, slicing through tank hulls like food packaging. Devourer Titans lack the subtlety of their smaller cousins, but few can doubt their effectiveness as predators.

specialRules.name: Unwieldy
specialRules.description: Strikes last when charging.

specialRules.name: Imprecise
specialRules.description: Gets -1 to hit when attacking.

specialRules.name: Predator
specialRules.description: For each unmodified roll of 6 to hit when attacking, this model may roll +1 attack with that weapon. This rule doesn’t apply to newly generated attacks.

specialRules.name: Infiltrate
specialRules.description: Counts as having Ambush, but may be deployed anywhere over 3" away from enemy unit.

specialRules.name: Crossing Attack
specialRules.description: Once per activation, when this model moves through enemy units, pick one of them and roll X dice. For each 6+ the target takes one wound.

specialRules.name: Increased Shooting Range
specialRules.description: This model gets +6" range when shooting.

specialRules.name: Hive Bond
specialRules.description: If most models in this unit have this rule, the first time they are attacked each round, they get +1 to Morale Test rolls.

specialRules.name: Precise
specialRules.description: Gets +1 to hit when attacking.

specialRules.name: Unique Hero
specialRules.description: This hero may only be taken once per party.

specialRules.name: Regenerative Strength
specialRules.description: Place one token on this model when it ignores a wound. Once per round, when it’s this model’s turn to strike in melee, roll as many dice as tokens on it before attacking, unless this unit is Fatigued. For each 4+ the target takes one wound.

specialRules.name: Rapid Charge
specialRules.description: This model moves +4" when using Charge actions.

specialRules.name: Enhanced Hive Bond
specialRules.description: If most models in this unit have Hive Bond, they always get +1 to Morale Test rolls from Hive Bond (instead of only the first time they are attacked each round).

specialRules.name: Hit & Run Fighter
specialRules.description: Once per round, this model may move by up to 3" after being in melee.

specialRules.name: Stealth Buff
specialRules.description: Only one use per game. Once per activation, before attacking, pick up to 3 friendly units within 12", which gets Stealth once (next time the effect would apply).

specialRules.name: Ignores Cover
specialRules.description: This weapon ignores Cover.

specialRules.name: Spell Conduit
specialRules.description: Casters within 12" that are from other friendly units may cast spells as if they were in this model's position, and get +1 to casting rolls when doing so. Friendly casters may only use this rule if this unit isn't Shaken.

specialRules.name: Spell Resistance
specialRules.description: When a unit where most models have this rule takes wounds, roll one die for each. On a 6+ it is ignored. If the wounds were from a spell, then they are ignored on a 2+ instead.

specialRules.name: Piercing Target
specialRules.description: Only one use per game. Once per game, during this model's activation, pick X enemy units within 18" and in line of sight of it, and place one token on them. Friendly units get AP(+1) on their weapons when attacking them.

specialRules.name: Precision Debuff
specialRules.description: Only one use per game. Once per activation, before attacking, pick up to 3 enemy units within 18" in line of sight, which gets -1 to hit rolls when attacking once (next time the effect would apply).

specialRules.name: Piercing Growth
specialRules.description: Place one marker on this unit at the beginning of each round if it's on the table and isn't Shaken, up to a max. of six markers. For every three markers, models with this rule in this unit get AP(+1). All markers are removed once the next wave of reinforcements is deployed.

specialRules.name: Spawn
specialRules.description: Add a friendly AI unit of X to the party, which is deployed as if it were a hero. This unit is activated after all Heroes, and follows the AI activation rules.

specialRules.name: Takedown Strike
specialRules.description: Once per game, when it's this model's turn to strike in melee, it may make X attacks at Quality 2+ with AP(2), Deadly(3), and Takedown.

specialRules.name: Surprise Attack
specialRules.description: Only one use per game. Counts as having Infiltrate. The first time this unit is activated, pick one enemy unit within 6" in line of sight, and roll X dice. For each 2+ it takes one hit with AP(1).

specialRules.name: Ignores Regeneration
specialRules.description: This weapon ignores Regeneration.

specialRules.name: Crossing Strike
specialRules.description: Once per activation, when this model moves through enemy units, pick one of them and attack it with this weapon as if it was shooting. This weapon may only be used in this way.

specialRules.name: Fragment
specialRules.description: When attacking units where most models have Defense 4+ to Defense 6+, the target must re-roll successful unmodified Defense results of 4-6.

specialRules.name: Unpredictable Fighter
specialRules.description: When in melee, roll one die and apply one effect to all models with this rule: on a 1-3 they get AP(+1), and on a 4-6 they get +1 to hit rolls instead.

specialRules.name: Furious Buff
specialRules.description: Only one use per game. Once per activation, before attacking, pick up to 3 friendly units within 12", which gets Furious once (next time the effect would apply).

specialRules.name: Unpredictable Fighter Mark
specialRules.description: Only one use per game. Once per activation, before attacking, pick up to 3 enemy units within 18" in line of sight, which friendly units gets Unpredictable Fighter against once (next time the effect would apply).

specialRules.name: Valiant
specialRules.description: If most models in this unit have this rule, the first time they are attacked each round, they get +1 to Morale Test rolls.

specialRules.name: Enhanced Valiant
specialRules.description: If most models in this unit have Valiant, they always get +1 to Morale Test rolls from Valiant (instead of only the first time they are attacked each round).

specialRules.name: Ambush
specialRules.description: May be set aside before deployment. At the start of any round after the first, may be placed anywhere over 9” away from enemy units.

specialRules.name: Hero
specialRules.description: Units within 6” of friendly Heroes may use the Hero’s Quality for Morale Tests as long as the Hero isn’t Shaken.

specialRules.name: Stealth
specialRules.description: When units where most models have this rule are shot from over 9" away, enemy units get -1 to hit rolls.

specialRules.name: Caster
specialRules.description: Gets X spell tokens at the start of each round, but can’t have more than 6 at once. Once per activation, before attacking, spend as many tokens as the spell’s value to try casting one or more spells (only one try per spell). Pick a target and roll one die, and on 4+ resolve the spell’s effect. Heroes may spend any number of tokens/power before rolling to get +1 to the roll per token/power, or to give an enemy Caster within 18” -1 to their roll per token/power.

specialRules.name: AP
specialRules.description: Targets get -X to Defense rolls when blocking hits.

specialRules.name: Takedown
specialRules.description: This model may pick any model in the target unit as its individual target for this weapon's attacks, which is resolved as if it was a unit of [1]. Takedown attacks must be resolved before other weapons.

specialRules.name: Deadly
specialRules.description: Assign each wound to one model, and multiply it by X. Hits from Deadly must be resolved first, and these wounds don’t carry over to other models if the original target is killed.

specialRules.name: Regeneration
specialRules.description: When a unit where most models have this rule takes wounds, roll one die for each. On a 5+ it is ignored.

specialRules.name: Defense
specialRules.description: This model gets +X to Defense rolls.

specialRules.name: Furious
specialRules.description: When charging, unmodified result of 6 to hit deal 1 extra hit (only the original hit counts as a 6 for special rules).

specialRules.name: Unpredictable
specialRules.description: When attacking, roll one die and apply one effect to all models with this rule: on a 1-3 they get AP(+1), and on a 4-6 they get +1 to hit rolls instead.
